question.problem: The dimensions of a cubic water tank are $2.4\,\text{m}\times 2.4\,\text{m}\times 2.4\,\text{m},$  where each dimension is measured to the nearest $0.1\,\text{m}.$ Rounded to the nearest tenth of a cubic meter, what is the smallest possible volume of the tank?
question.worked_solution:
Each dimension is given to the nearest $0.1\,\text{m}.$ So, the greatest possible error of these measurements is

$$
\frac{0.1\,\text{m}}{2}=0.05\,\text{m}.
$$

We wish to find the *smallest* possible volume of the tank. Therefore, we require the *lower bound* of each dimension.

The lower bounds for each dimension are as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & 2.4\,\text{m}-0.05\,\text{m}=2.35\,\text{m} \\  & 2.4\,\text{m}-0.05\,\text{m}=2.35\,\text{m} \\  & 2.4\,\text{m}-0.05\,\text{m}=2.35\,\text{m}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the smallest possible volume of the tank is

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2.35\,\text{m}\times 2.35\,\text{m}\times 2.35\,\text{m} \\  & =12.977\,875\,{\text{m}}^{3} \\  & ≈13.0\,{\text{m}}^{3},\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest tenth of a cubic meter.
